summary: In Greek mythology, Echion (Ancient Greek Ἐχίων, from ἔχις, "viper") of Alope is a son of Hermes and Antianeira (or Laothoe), twin or brother of Erytus (Eurytus), and an Argonaut. Apollonius and Pindar number him among Jason's crew; Hyginus and Ovid also place him at the Calydonian boar hunt. He is distinct from Echion the Theban Spartos.

sections.heading: Son of Hermes
paragraphs: Echion of Alope was son of Hermes by Antianeira daughter of Menetus, or by Laothoe in a variant; his brother was Erytus (also Eurytus), and Aethalides is sometimes named as a stepbrother. As children of the thief-god, Apollonius describes Echion and Erytus as "well skilled in craftiness."

sections.heading: Argonaut and boar hunter
paragraphs: Pindar (Pythian 4) and Apollonius Rhodius (Argonautica 1.51–56) list Echion among the Argonauts who sailed from Alope. Hyginus (Fabulae 14, 173) and Ovid (Metamorphoses 8.311) also count him among the hunters of the Calydonian boar.
Beyond these catalogue appearances he has little separate myth; his fame is genealogical and crew-list rather than episodic.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (echion-hermes) is the Argonaut son of Hermes. Distinct from Echion the Spartos of Thebes, husband of Agave and father of Pentheus (echion); from a Giant of that name; from a Greek at Troy said to have died leaping from the Wooden Horse; and from a Dulichian suitor of Penelope (echion-dulichium).
